item.title: Get involved
item.description:
Kompass is a new political initiative. We are looking for people who would like to contribute with ideas, knowledge and practical work.

For example, you could help with:

  • political ideas and fact-checking
  • writing and communication
  • organisation and administration
  • public outreach
  • practical work during the election campaign

You do not need previous experience in politics. What matters is that you share our ambition to contribute to a more optimistic political conversation in Sweden.

item.title: How to vote
item.description:
Elections to the Riksdag, the regional assemblies and the municipal assemblies will take place on 13 September 2026.

For complete and official information about voting, visit the Swedish Election Authority.

Who has the right to vote?

You have the right to vote in the election to the Riksdag if you:

  • are at least 18 years old on election day
  • are a Swedish citizen
  • are or have previously been listed in the Swedish Population Register

You may also have the right to vote in the municipal and regional elections without Swedish citizenship:

item.title: Is Kompass for you?
item.description:
This is not a scientific survey or a recommendation on how you should vote. It is a simple way to compare your starting points with those of Kompass.

Your answers remain in your browser and are not sent to Kompass.

item.title: Starting points
item.description:
Kompass believes that Sweden is built every day by those of us who live and work here. The building blocks are dreams and work. We build together.

Growth, work and taxation

Economic growth matters, but longevity and health matter even more.

It should pay to work, but we must share too.

It is we who must pay taxes, not someone else.

Raising taxes cannot solve every new challenge.

Our shared challenges are growing in healthcare, education, infrastructure and security. The room for tax cuts is limited.

item.title: Why Kompass?
item.description:
There are eight parties in the Swedish Riksdag, all represented by experienced and hard-working politicians. Surely everyone should be able to find a party among them that suits them? Probably. But what troubles us is the political conversation itself: the harsh tone and the pessimism, as though we did not belong together and were not already achieving many good things together.

That is why we decided to raise our voices, in a friendly and optimistic tone. We also decided to listen carefully, because a good conversation requires us to listen more than we speak, at least when there are more than two people involved. We believe that a constructive and optimistic political conversation is the way forward.
